business_problem: The Public Sector Fraud Authority sought to detect suspicious networks and fraudulent claims involving public funds, including organised crime and sanctions evasion.
solution_summary: The Public Sector Fraud Authority’s Single Network Analytics Platform (SNAP), launched through a £4 million partnership with Quantexa, is an AI-powered tool for public-sector fraud detection. The upgrade adds three collections to SNAP: UK and US sanctions records, World Bank debarments, and UK dormant-company records. The source says these records are added to the tool to help detect suspicious networks, activity, and users; it does not describe the ingestion mechanism, processing architecture, storage technology, model design, or hosting topology. SNAP makes the resulting information available to relevant public bodies, which can review it and take action. The tool supports detection of fraudulent claims on public funds through contracts, grants, and loans, as well as organised crime and sanctions evasion. The story describes the data additions and investigative use, but does not name further system integrations or operational workflows.

solution_components.name: Single Network Analytics Platform (SNAP)
solution_components.role: The AI-powered fraud detection tool uses added sanctions, debarment, and dormant-company records to identify suspicious networks, activity, and users.

solution_components.name: Quantexa
solution_components.role: Quantexa is the AI technology partner in the partnership through which SNAP was launched.

data_flow: UK and US sanctions entities, World Bank debarments, and UK dormant-company records are added to SNAP; the AI fraud-detection tool uses the expanded data to identify suspicious networks, activity, and users. Relevant public-sector bodies then review the information and take action.
integration_points: Relevant public-sector bodies reviewing flagged information
business_outcome: The added records are intended to help public-sector organisations detect fraudulent claims and identify suspicious networks, organised crime, and sanctions evasion for further investigation.

source_references.title: “Criminals should be aware” says Minister as Government upgrades AI fraud detection tool

evidence_quotes: The Government’s AI-powered fraud detection tool – the Single Network Analytics Platform (SNAP) – has been upgraded with thousands of new sanctions and debarment records.
This information can then be used by the relevant bodies to review and take action.
